title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside Grothendieck's long computation in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The setting is a family of groups attached to a pair (ρ,σ) of finite-order 'avatars'. Most likely these are the order-2 and order-3 torsion elements relevant to the loop equations of the Teichmüller tower / Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

The groups involved:
- γ_{ρ,σ} is a finite group.
- Z_{ρ,σ}, N*_ρ, N*_σ, C_{ρ,σ} (or G_{ρ,σ}) each map to γ_{ρ,σ} via δ-maps.
- The kernels of these maps are L_0 (for Z), SN*_ρ and SN*_σ.

The previous page defined the iterated fibre products over γ:
- M = N*_ρ ×_γ N*_σ ×_γ C
- S_0M = Z ×_γ M
- Γ = N*_ρ ×_γ N*_σ
- S_0Γ = Z ×_γ Γ

It also gave exact sequences in which 𝔖^+ is the kernel of M→Γ.

On this page Grothendieck records three consequences of associativity of fibre products:
- (57) S_0M ≃ M ×_γ Z
- (58) S_0Γ ≃ Γ ×_γ Z
- (59) S_0M ≃ M ×_Γ S_0Γ

In words: Z_{ρ,σ} is an extension of γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0, and the extensions S_0M, S_0Γ of M, Γ by L_0 are its pullbacks along M→γ and Γ→γ. Also, S_0M is the pullback of the extension S_0Γ along M→Γ (transitivity of pullback).

He then introduces an element τ'_M = (τ'_ρ, τ'_σ, τ'_G). Its components are the 'avatars' of a fixed element τ' taken in N*_ρ, N*_σ and G_{ρ,σ} respectively. These have the same image in γ_{ρ,σ}, so they define an element of the fibre product M_{ρ,σ}. This gives a homomorphism (61) 𝔖^+ → M_{ρ,σ}, τ' ↦ τ'_M. It identifies 𝔖^+ with its image, presumably the kernel 𝔖^+ ⊂ M from sequence (54).

The crossed-out text shows he first intended to list all homomorphisms and relations in commutative diagrams. He did that on the next page as the cube-shaped diagram (62).

The purpose is bookkeeping: assembling the normalizer/centralizer data of finite subgroups into one coherent diagram of extensions. This serves the analysis of the loop equations and of the torsion in the relevant (profinite) groups.
errors: No mathematical error. (57)–(59) follow formally from associativity and transitivity of fibre products / pullbacks of extensions.
Calling these 'extensions by L_0' requires Z_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ} to be surjective with kernel ≃ L_0. Page 583's (50)–(55) assert this.

The phrase 'la même image dans γ_{ρ,σ} et a fortiori dans γ_{ρ,σ}' repeats the same group. Either one occurrence is a different group (e.g. a quotient), or it is a slip of the pen or of the transcription.
In (59) the left-hand side looks like 'SM' or 'ℓM'. To match (52) and the next page's diagram it must be S_0M_{ρ,σ}.

ideas.what: Expressing the groups S_0M, S_0Γ as pullbacks of a single extension Z_{ρ,σ} of the finite group γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0, plus transitivity of pullback (59).
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of group extensions (Baer pullback); fibre products of groups
ideas.where_published: Not in the published texts; this specific setting is part of the unpublished 'équation des lacets' notes.

ideas.what: Defining a diagonal element τ'_M from compatible avatars of τ' in N*_ρ, N*_σ, G_{ρ,σ}, and hence an embedding 𝔖^+ → M_{ρ,σ}.
ideas.modern_name: Induced homomorphism into a fibre product (universal property)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of fibre products and pullbacks of extensions within a larger unpublished computation. There is no new result or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: In (61) and in 'ses Ẑ^+', the symbol is the stylised gothic 𝔖 (as in 𝔖^+ on the previous and next pages), not Ẑ^+. (61) should read 𝔖^+ --τ'_M--> M_{ρ,σ}, identifying 𝔖^+ via τ' ↦ τ'_M.
In (57)/(58) the subscripted group is Z_{ρ,σ} (a struck capital Z) in both formulas. In (58), Γ_{ρ,σ} carries a corrected subscript.
In (59) the left side should be read S_0M_{ρ,σ}, and the fibre product is over Γ_{ρ,σ}.
'dont l'opposé[?]' likely reads 'dont l'application de 𝔖^+' or similar. The sentence says the resulting map 𝔖^+ → M is the one given by τ (τ').
Line (60) originally began 'τ'_M ∈ S_0M_{ρ,σ}'. This was struck and replaced by 'On introduit un élément τ'_M = (τ'_ρ, τ'_σ, τ'_G)', with small letters a, b, c written above the components.
